status: Experimental implementation verified; default promotion withheld

contract.cpu: Resumable IN/OUT at I/O T2 after 9 nominal cycles; one-cycle Tw steps; one T3 and one register access on release; interrupt acceptance deferred.
contract.board: PROVISIONAL: matching active transfer waits while BUSY=1 and DRQ=0, releases on DRQ or command completion; no status-register observation.
contract.controller: Existing byte pacing enabled; write-sector lead-in override disabled in experimental builds; shared WD179x source unchanged.
contract.drive: Functional 300 RPM index source, 2 ms pulse, no motor spin-up or flux model.

validation.cpu_ready_tests: PASS immediate and 0..49 wait cycles for IN/OUT, exact-once side effects, EI/interrupt deferral, indefinite wait and reset
validation.machine_tests: PASS sector reads/writes at both controller clocks; preload/pacing; remount; Read Address; Read Track; multiple-record reads/writes; Write Track formatting; missing ID; lost data; force abort; write protection; not ready; bounded stepping; pending IRQ
validation.snapshots: PASS native and WASM: pending IN/OUT save/restore, execution chunk invariance, reset cancellation, cross-configuration rejection
validation.default_native: make test PASS, including Kaypro controller regression
validation.sanitizers: AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer machine tests PASS

full_board.limitation: Inherited boot bench forces READY high; runnable board also ties D94 A4 high.

hdl.full_board_observation: Run stopped at the 100000 VRAM-write bound with zero FDC data reads, one FDC status read, zero raw I/O writes, and motor off. No firmware sector loop reached. Cause not diagnosed by this change.
forced_boundaries: runnable juku_top ties D94 A4 high
boot harness does not enable FDC_BYTE_TIMING
hdl.focused_bench: Captured D94 table matches all 32 decoded rows; A4 gates data read/write strobes. Externally stimulated D2/D30 READY stalls VM80A through one IN and one OUT with 40 wait phases; not a board-wiring proof.

independent_sources.use: Read/write DRQ, status acknowledgment, lost-data continuation and 22-byte MFM write lead interval. Does not specify Juku CPU synchronization.

Independent functional state-machine comparison only. STATE_READ loads read_timer=15 and watchdog uses 4096 CPU-enable events; not accepted as a Juku physical byte-timing oracle. No third-party code copied.
